extracted.intended_audience: broadcast licensees, base station operators, FM applicants/petitioners, and parties filing comments in FCC rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for operation of PELTS base stations (antenna height, control, tests, identification, records, interconnection) and procedural rules for participating in FCC notice-and-comment proceedings on FM channel allotments (deadlines, service, ex parte limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antenna height considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: A base station antenna (the station’s radiating structure, including tower/mast/pole and attachments) must not be a hazard to aircraft; licensee must obtain FCC permission before the uppermost tip may be higher than permitted by paragraphs (b), (c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum allowed heights regardless of other requirements: (1) at least 6.1 meters (20 feet) above ground or mounting structure; or (2) equal to height of an existing antenna to which attached. Antenna may be as high as 61 meters (200 feet) above ground unless within 6.1 kilometers (20,000 feet) of an airport or heliport. Near airports/heliports listed in FAA Airport Facilities Directory or DOD-operated, height limits are set by formulas: (1) 1 meter higher than airport elevation per 100 meters from nearest runway if runway >1 km and within 6.1 km; (2) 2 meters higher per 100 meters if runway ≤1 km and within 3.1 km; (3) 4 meters higher per 100 meters for heliport if pad within 1.5 km. If FCC grants permission to exceed normal limits, licensee may be required to mark the antenna with bright paint and light it at night (see part 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and FAA notification for excess antenna height
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for a new or modified base station seeking permission for an antenna higher than normally allowed must request on FCC Form 574 and notify the Federal Aviation Administration on FAA Form 7466-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both filing of the FCC request (Form 574) and notification to FAA are mandatory procedural prerequisites to obtain FCC permission for exceedance of normal antenna height limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Servicing, maintenance, and qualified supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee is responsible for proper operation of the station at all times and must provide observations, servicing and maintenance as often as necessary; adjustments or tests during installation/servicing/maintenance should be performed by or under the immediate supervision and responsibility of a person certified as technically qualified by an organization or committee representative of users in private land mobile and fixed services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include routine observation and maintenance to ensure proper operation; certification of technicians should be from an appropriate representative organization/committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test transmission rules during internal adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, test signals during internal adjustments must use a non-radiating simulated antenna; brief test signals using a radiating antenna may be transmitted but must not exceed one minute during any five-minute period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radiating test transmissions may be used to adjust the antenna or detect/measure spurious radiation, but they shall not interfere with ongoing communications, must be properly identified as required, and may otherwise be unmodulated as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: General licensee duties and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee is responsible for proper operation of the station at all times and must have access to the station equipment and be able to disable it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee must ensure personnel/arrangements exist to access and disable equipment to maintain compliance or address problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible communications by channel and emergency priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific channels are limited to defined uses: channels 1, 2, 6, and 7 — emergency assistance voice communications involving safety of life and property; channel 3 — one-way non-commercial informational voice messages (weather, hazards, closings, rest stops, first-aid locations); channels 4, 5, 8, and 9 — short distance personal voice communications; channel 10 — non-voice emergency alerting/homing transmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority must be given to emergency communications; communications not pertinent to constructive handling of an emergency are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited transmissions content
rubrics_metrics.description: PELTS stations are not authorized to communicate: (1) messages connected with activity against Federal, state or local law; (2) false or deceptive messages; (3) intentional interference; (4) music, whistling, sound effects, or other transmissions to amuse, entertain, or attract attention; (5) obscene, profane, or indecent language; (6) advertisements or offers for sale of goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These content prohibitions apply across permitted channels and are absolute restrictions on PELTS station transmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every PELTS base station must transmit a station identification following the transmission of communications or a series of communications, and every 15 minutes during a long transmission; the identification is the call sign assigned to the base station (a unit number may be included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification must be clearly transmitted by voice in English, with each letter and digit separately and distinctly transmitted (letters may be said using a phonetic alphabet per ITU Radio Regulations, Appendix 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Station recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must keep station records for the base station during the license term (except expired authorizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records include, where applicable: a copy of the current license, copies of letters to FCC about name/mailing changes, copies of answers to discrepancy notices, grant of Special Temporary Authority (STA) or waivers, copy of any renewal application pending action, and copy of FCC consent to corporate control changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station inspection compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an authorized FCC representative wishes to inspect any station or station records, the licensee or station operator must make the station available for inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee/operator must facilitate inspections and provide requested records during inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station control point and operator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each base station must have a control point where the station operator can communicate messages and control the station by causing it to transmit and cease transmitting; taking necessary and reasonable precautions to assure unauthorized/improper operations do not occur; refraining from transmissions that may reasonably be expected to cause improper operation of others' equipment; and obeying Commission-imposed additional requirements in cases of recurrent interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The control point must be at the station unless the license authorizes remote control from another point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote control and control link requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A station operator may control a base station from a remote point through a control link which must be either a wireline control link (solely for transmitter control for messages conveyed by the control link and transmitted by the base station) or a radio control link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remotely controlled stations must not make unauthorized transmissions; the operator must perform required duties when controlling remotely; if the control link fails such that the operator cannot perform duties, the remotely controlled station must not transmit. The FCC does not consider a station remotely controlled if the connection is wireless or mechanical and the station and control point are on the same vehicle or at the same street address or within 152 meters (500 feet) of each other. Any device used to establish a wireline control link attached to the public switched telephone network must be registered with the FCC and comply with standards in the registration program to protect the PSTN (see part 68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interconnection prohibition and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: No station in the PELTS may be interconnected to the public switched telephone network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wireline or radio circuits/links furnished by common carriers used by licensees or authorized persons for transmitter control (including dial-up transmitter control circuits) or as an integral part of an authorized private internal system of communication are not considered interconnected for purposes of this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment filing procedures and deadlines for FCC NPRMs
rubrics_metrics.description: For Notices of Proposed Rule Making on channel allotments, interested parties must file comments with the FCC by the specified comment date and file reply comments by the specified reply date; in addition to filing with the FCC, interested parties should serve the petitioner's counsel or specified representative at the address listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each NPRM lists the comment and reply-comment deadlines (e.g., comments by February 12, 1990; reply comments by February 27, 1990) and provides the petitioner’s counsel contact for service. For proper filing procedures see 47 CFR 1.415 and 1.420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contact restriction during channel-allotment proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: From the time a Notice of Proposed Rule Making is issued until the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review, all ex parte contacts are prohibited in Commission proceedings that involve channel allotments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 47 CFR 1.1204(b) for rules governing permissible ex parte contact; parties should avoid prohibited communications during the pendency of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing expressions of interest and channel allocation procedural treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 47 CFR 1.420(g), competing expressions of interest in use of an allotted channel will not be considered and the petitioner will not be required to demonstrate the availability of an additional equivalent channel for use by such interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain channel substitutions/allotments are announced with this limitation, meaning the Commission will not entertain competing expressions for that channel in the specified proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site restrictions, minimum distance separations, and international concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel allotments must comply with the Commission’s minimum distance separation requirements; site restrictions may be applied to avoid short-spacing (e.g., a 6.6 km site restriction to avoid short-spacing to another station). Canadian concurrence will be requested for allotments located within 320 kilometers of the U.S.-Canadian border.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination or concurrence may be required for border-area allotments; site restrictions may be used to accommodate desired transmitter sites while meeting spacing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation for noncommercial educational use and Regulatory Flexibility Act note
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposed channel allotments may be reserved for noncommercial educational use; provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 do not apply to certain of these proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an allotment is proposed for reservation (e.g., reservation of Channel *276C to Helena for noncommercial educational use), the NPRM will state that reservation and whether Regulatory Flexibility Act provisions apply.
